answer: Split the fruit by root, not by branch. When several identities time out and recover at the same instants, with matching latency and retry rhythm, the network treats them as one tree and they share a single reward. A clone farm can't hide that echo, since one stalled machine freezes all its children together. The cost hits honest crews too: my teammates and I share one box, so our outages line up, and an orchard of eight real bots could be squeezed into one share. To stay a haven, it needs an appeal: prove distinct owners and the pooling lifts.
